title: Hosted API cost levers prioritization matrix
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet prioritizes cost-reduction levers for Hosted API unit economics (token COGS, margin by model and region). It is intentionally operational: mix of spreadsheets, pragmatic experiments, and a short runbook to move quick dollars.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Biggest near-term wins (low dev effort, high impact): autosuggested batching policy tweaks for 2x common short-request flows; regional ratecard reweighting to avoid high-cost zones for non-enterprise customers; token-level inference caching for common prompts.
- Medium-term (moderate effort): per-model quantization profiles + fallbacks; per-customer routing rules based on cost-sensitivity tags.
- Longer-term (higher effort): mixed-precision kernel adoption across all T5-like models, and redesign of streaming path to enable incremental dispatching for prefix-heavy workloads.

Quick map (impact vs complexity):
CSV: lever,impact_estimate_usd_month,engineering_complexity,owner,priority
batching-policy-2x-short-requests,~$120k,low,eng-serving-runtime,high
regional-ratecard-weighting,~$95k,low,product-ops,high
token-prefix-caching,~$80k,medium,eng-serving-runtime,high
per-model-quant-profiles,~$65k,medium,applied-ml,medium
function-call-cost-sandboxing,~$20k,medium,platform-engineering,low
kernel-mixed-precision-rollout,~$200k,high,release-engineering,low

Assumptions for numbers above:
- Baseline monthly hosted tokens (prod) ~ 200B tokens across all customers (mix H2 2024).
- Pricing/margin assumptions: average price $0.0006 / token for generation tiers (weighted), current average COGS baseline $0.00018 / token.
- Impact estimate = conservative % reduction in per-token COGS * monthly token volume for affected workloads.

Per-model / region snapshot (sample rows pulled from payback workbook):
CSV: model,region,gpu_type,baseline_cogs_per_1k_tokens_usd,notes
redwood-7b-v1,us-west1,A10G,0.18,cheap on A10G but poor batching for short chats
openchat-13b,eu-west1,A100-80GB,0.95,high mem, high KV overhead for long contexts
llama2-70b,asia-southeast1,H100,1.85,expensive in APAC due to fewer zones
redwood-2.7b,us-east1,A10G,0.09,common for embeddings/short completions

Suggested targeted levers (detail):
1) Batching-policy tuning for short completions
- Observed: 60% of requests are < 64 tokens, 75% of these are independent single-turn queries (chat). Current batching timeout conservative (10ms) which hurts throughput for small tokens.
- Experiment: for requests tagged short (<=64 tokens) try 20ms aggregate window + dynamic pack-by-length. Expected: 1.8-2.2x throughput improvement on p95 and ~40-50% token-cost reduction for that cohort.
- Minimal rollout: canary on a slice of non-enterprise keys (5%), measure latency SLA violations and cost delta.
- JIRA: JIRA-OPT-2213 (experiment); Owner: eng-serving-runtime (Diego).

2) Regional routing weight shifts for non-SLA traffic
- Idea: by default route cost-insensitive traffic to lower-cost regions (us-central / us-west) while keeping enterprise/fallback in region of request. Implement routing policy that considers: customer-tier tag, latency budget, and regulatory flag.
- Quick wins: move 25% of non-SLA traffic from eu-west1 & apac to us-west1 -> estimated $95k/month.
- Risks: increased latency for some customers; need to surface opt-out via Console.

3) Token-prefix cache for common prompts (shared prompt caches)
- Implement a small LRU-shard on KV cache to persist prefix computations for frequently hit system prompts and template instructions.
- Measurement plan: identify top 1k prompt templates via usage logs; simulate cache hit rate. Expected 10-25% COGS savings for long-context customer mixes.

4) Per-model quantization profiles and auto-fallback
- Build a short-run eval harness to profile each model under INT8/4-bit quant profiles with sample QA/LLM tests to ensure quality not degraded beyond threshold. Create rollback policy if hallucination score increases.
- Integration: hook into model catalog so for each model we have: recommended_quant_profile, expected_token_savings_pct.

5) Operational: rate-based throttles on tail requests
- Implement soft throttles for extremely long contexts ( > 8k tokens) for free/low-tier customers, with clear error messaging and a paid-path link. Expected to reduce 1% of total token volume but 6-8% of COGS concentrated in tail.

Prioritization rubric (how we scored levers):
- Impact (monetary): monthly USD impact estimate
- Effort: engineering + infra + Q/A time (low/medium/high) translated to estimated weeks
- Risk: customer-facing risk (service, quality) low/med/high
- Score = impact_rank - effort_penalty - risk_penalty (internal scoring used to order list).

Short experimental runbook (steps to ship a low-risk lever):
1) Create feature flag and canary cohort (5% non-enterprise).
2) Instrument: per-token counters, per-request latency, success/error codes, and token-Cogs estimate.
3) 72-hour canary run, sample every 12 hours; if cost delta > 15% and latency SLO breaches < 1% then expand to 25%.
4) Postmortem: if expansion triggers SLO > 1% or customer complaints > threshold, rollback and record lessons learned.

Data sources and queries (start points):
- analytics:ga:hosted_api_token_usage_by_model (daily)
- infra:prometheus:inflight-batch-sizes, serving-runtime:kv-hit-ratio
- logs:bigquery:prod_requests.prompt_templates_top_1000
- retention window: 90d for sample size

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Pricing guardrails: what minimum margin do we require per model-region before we consider aggressive routing? (Product ops decision)
- Console UX: opt-out for routing change — product design needed ASAP to avoid support friction.
- Legal/regulatory: any data residency rules that block routing for a customer? Need a whitelist of regs to consult.

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Diego to spin up 2x batching canary for short-requests (JIRA-OPT-2213).
- Priya to run region-origin simulation using last 30d logs to estimate latency delta for routing reweights (CONFLUENCE-5602).
- Miguel to draft a brief for GTM/sales on potential savings and opt-out story (ETA: 2024-11-22).

Appendix: quick numeric worked example (short-requests batching)
- Suppose cohort volume = 20B tokens/month, baseline COGS cohort = $0.00016/token. If batching reduces COGS by 50% for that cohort -> savings = 20B * 0.00008 = $1.6M/month (this is theoretical max; we used conservative $120k in prioritization because production constraints and partial rollout).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Pull last 90d per-customer token distribution and identify top 10% customers that drive 70% of tail COGS.
- Add a simple sheet to the workbook that converts per-request p95 latency delta into estimated revenue churn risk (mappings from GTM).
- Align with security on cache designs (shared prompt caches must not leak customer-provided system prompts).

Sign-off: Miguel Ortega (product-optimize).
